title: Gmail for documentary filmmakers on Mac: shortcuts, templates and sending large cuts
metaTitle: Gmail for Documentary Filmmakers on Mac: Shortcuts and Tips
description: Gmail for documentary filmmakers on Mac: turn on shortcuts, save reply templates, undo sends and get past the 25 MB attachment limit in Safari or Chrome.

intro: Gmail for documentary filmmakers on Mac works best in Safari or Chrome, with keyboard shortcuts turned on and your common replies saved as templates. Google does not offer a Gmail app for Mac, so the browser is your main route. This page covers the settings that save the most time, the 25 MB attachment limit, and where Lazur helps.
tldr: Turn on keyboard shortcuts first: gear icon > See all settings > Keyboard shortcuts, then Save Changes.
Save the replies you send often as templates. Templates work only in Gmail on your computer, not the phone app.
Undo Send gives you 5, 10, 20 or 30 seconds to stop a send. It does not recall a message that has been delivered.
A personal Gmail account sends attachments up to 25 MB. Bigger files go out as Google Drive links instead.
Lazur points, guides, explains and drafts text in Gmail. It does not click buttons or send your mail for you.

blocks.text: Gmail runs in a browser on your Mac. Google does not offer an official Gmail desktop app for macOS, according to clean.email's 2026 guide to Gmail apps for Mac. So you open Gmail in Safari or Chrome and set it up there. Most of the time savings on this page come from settings you change once.
Pick one browser and keep Gmail open in it

Pick the browser you already use for production work. Safari and Chrome both run Gmail well. If your cut notes, call sheets and Drive folders already live in one browser, put Gmail there too. Fewer windows means less hunting for the right tab.

Chrome profiles help if you run a production account and a personal account. Each profile keeps its own sign in, bookmarks and extensions. Open the profile icon in Chrome's toolbar to switch between them.

Pinning Gmail to the Dock saves a few clicks each day. The steps for Safari and Chrome are in [How to pin Gmail to Dock on Mac](/how-to/pin-gmail-to-the-dock-in-gmail). Gmail still runs in your browser, so keep that browser signed in.
Turn on Gmail keyboard shortcuts on Mac before anything else

Gmail shortcuts are off by default. Turn them on once, and they stay on. Click the gear icon, choose See all settings, then open the Keyboard shortcuts section. Pick Keyboard shortcuts on, and click Save Changes.

On a Mac, Gmail uses ⌘ where Windows uses Ctrl. Press ⇧ + / at any time to open the shortcut list inside Gmail. The table below covers the shortcuts that matter most for review threads and producer notes.

blocks.caption: Gmail shortcuts that save the most time on review threads.

blocks.text: Single-letter keys such as e and r only work when your cursor is not in a message box. If a letter appears in the text, click outside the box first.

blocks.title: Enter sends at once
blocks.text: ⌘ + Enter sends the message right away. Read the draft before you press it. If you send the wrong one, Undo Send is your only quick way back.
Save Gmail templates for emails you write every week

Many film jobs repeat the same emails. A release form request, a cut approval note, a follow up to a festival programmer and a music clearance question all keep their shape. Write each one once, save it, and insert it into a new message when you need it.
Templates are off by default. Turn them on in the gear icon > See all settings > Advanced tab. Find Templates, click Enable, then click Save Changes.

items: Write the email in a new message. Use plain placeholders for the film name and the date of the next cut.
Click More options (the three dots at the bottom of the compose window) > Templates > Save draft as template > Save as new template.
Give it a name you will recognize later, such as Release form request.
To use it, open a new message, then click More options > Templates > Insert template.
To update a template, change a draft, then choose Save draft as template and pick the old name under Overwrite Template.

blocks.title: Web only
blocks.text: Templates work only in Gmail on your computer. Google says templates are not in the Gmail mobile apps. Keep your most used text in a note on your phone, too.

Deleting a template is permanent. Google says you cannot recover it after you delete it. Copy the text into a note first. Google does not state a maximum number of templates, so build the list as you need it.
A useful first set covers release forms, cut approvals, festival follow ups and music clearance requests. Keep each template short. A long template is harder to edit for each new recipient.
A worked example: one cut approval from start to finish

Here is one common thread, start to finish. A producer sends a cut and asks for notes. You read it, reply with a template, schedule the reply for the editor's morning, and archive the thread once the notes arrive.

items: Open the thread and check the To and Cc lines. Press ⌘ + Shift + c if the editor needs a copy.
Press r to reply. Insert your cut approval template from More options > Templates > Insert template.
Change the cut name and the due day, then read the whole message once.
Schedule the reply for the editor's time zone, using the scheduling steps later in this guide.
After the notes arrive, apply the film's label and press e to archive the thread.

blocks.text: The sequence uses a few shortcuts, one template and one scheduled send. Once the settings are in place, each step takes seconds. The slow part is the reading, and no shortcut replaces that.
Undo Send in Gmail: what it does and what it cannot do

Undo Send is a short window after you press send. Open the gear icon > See all settings. Find Undo Send, then set the Send cancellation period to 5, 10, 20 or 30 seconds. For a cut, a contract or a payment note, pick 30 seconds.
After you send, a Message sent notice appears at the bottom left of the window. Click Undo in that notice to stop the send. Once the window closes, the message is on its way.

Undo Send does not recall a message that has already been delivered. Google's help page does not say what happens to delivered messages, so do not count on it. For that case, read [How to recall email in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/recall-a-sent-email-in-gmail).

blocks.title: Read first, then send
blocks.text: Treat the Undo window as a backup, not a plan. Read the To line and the attachments before you press ⌘ + Enter, even with a 30 second window.
Schedule send in Gmail for the hours your collaborators read mail
Scheduled send holds an email and sends it later. Google says a scheduled email can go out a few minutes after the time you choose. It follows the time zone you picked when you scheduled it.

This matters when your collaborators sit in another city. A sound mixer in another time zone should get your note at the start of their day, not yours. Pick their time zone when you schedule, then check the time shown before you confirm.
Two limits matter. Gmail holds up to 100 scheduled emails at once. To change a scheduled email, cancel it. Cancelling turns it into a draft, so you edit the draft and schedule it again.
Google's scheduling steps describe the iPhone and iPad app. For the browser steps, use [How to schedule email in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail).
Gmail attachment size limit 25 MB for cuts and rushes
The sending limit for a personal Gmail account is 25 MB. If the attachments add up to more than that, Gmail removes them and inserts a Google Drive link. The recipient gets a link, not the file.
Work and school accounts follow a limit that the Google Workspace administrator sets. Google's page does not give that number. Ask your administrator before you plan a big delivery.
A Drive link works only if the recipient can open it. Before you send, check the sharing setting on the file. Give the recipient access, and make sure the people on the thread can reach it.

items: Select the file in Finder and press ⌘ + i to see its size in Get Info.
If the attachments are over 25 MB on a personal account, upload them to a shared Drive folder.
Share the folder with the people on the thread, and check the access level before you send.
Put the link in the body of the email, with a line that says what the file is.
Keep the link in a note so you can find the same version next month.

blocks.text: Version names matter more than file size. Two links named final can look alike in a long thread. Name each delivery with the cut name and the date.
Keep the inbox short with labels, archive and filters
A single film can produce many threads across picture, sound, music and funding. Labels sort them by project. Create one label per film or one per department, then apply it to each thread.
Archive a finished thread with e. It leaves the inbox but stays searchable, so you can find it again under its label. Apply the label first, then archive, so the thread is easy to locate.

Filters can label new mail from a sender automatically. Set one up for your editor or your fund manager, and their mail lands under the right label. Follow [How to create a filter in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) for the browser steps.
For label steps, read [How to create a label in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail). Keep label names short, so they fit in the sidebar without wrapping.
Batch your email instead of checking it all day

A 2016 Microsoft Research study tracked 40 information workers for 12 workdays. The longer people spent on email each day, the lower their perceived productivity and the higher their measured stress. Batching was linked to higher perceived productivity, but not to lower stress.

That study covers office workers in general. It does not cover documentary filmmakers or Gmail. The pattern is still worth testing on your own schedule. Set a morning window and an afternoon window for mail, and close Gmail between them.
Shooting weeks break batching. A call sheet change at dawn is not a batch item. Keep a separate channel for urgent calls, such as a phone call or a text to the producer.

blocks.title: Mute the rest
blocks.text: Let only the people who can change your schedule reach you right away. Mute everyone else until your mail window opens.
Ask Lazur for the Gmail steps you keep looking up

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut.
Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves on.
Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Gmail. It does not click buttons or send mail for you. It shows you where things are and explains what they do, and you do the clicks.
Useful questions include where Undo Send lives, how to save a template, and what a Drive link in a thread means. Ask in plain words, the way you would ask a colleague across the room.

blocks.title: Ask at the right moment
blocks.text: Ask Lazur to point at the Undo link right after you send. The link appears only for the window you set.
Dictate long replies with fn, then fix the names
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Gmail's compose box counts as any app. Dictate the body of a long reply, then read it through before you press ⌘ + Enter.
Add the names and places you use often to your personal dictionary. Festival names, crew names and location names are good candidates. Add them once so dictation uses your spelling.
Snippets hold text you reuse, and clipboard slots hold text you copy between apps. A snippet works well for a standard credit line or a release form paragraph.
Dictation is good for a first draft. Read the result for names, dates and any figure in it, because a small error can go out in a reply.
Mistakes that slow down film email

items: Leaving shortcuts off, then clicking through every thread by hand.
Saving a template with an old cut name in it, then sending it again.
Attaching a large file, then finding the recipient got a link they cannot open.
Thinking Undo Send recalls a message after it has been delivered.
Scheduling a send in your own time zone when the recipient works in another.
Deleting a template to tidy up, with no copy of its text saved.

blocks.text: Each mistake has a short fix. Turn on the shortcuts, use placeholders for the cut name, set Drive sharing before you send, and check the time zone. Save a copy of any text you plan to delete.
What to do next in Gmail on your Mac

Start with the settings, because they take one visit. Turn on keyboard shortcuts, then turn on templates in the same settings screen. After that, save the replies you send most often. Check the Undo Send window and set it to a length you can live with.

Next, ask your administrator for the attachment limit on your work account, if you use one. Then set up one label per project and one filter for your most frequent sender. Ask Lazur to walk you through any step that stalls.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not an official one. According to clean.email's 2026 guide, Google does not offer an official Gmail desktop app for macOS. Use Safari or Chrome. Some guides describe installing Gmail as a Chrome web app, but those guides were not checked against Google's own help pages.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, in Gmail on your computer. Turn them on under the gear icon > See all settings > Advanced. Click Enable, then Save Changes. Google says templates are not in the Gmail mobile apps.

faq.question: How big can an attachment be in Gmail on Mac?
faq.answer: For a personal Gmail account, the sending limit is 25 MB. Larger attachments are removed and replaced with a Google Drive link. Work and school accounts use a limit that the administrator sets, and Google does not state that number.

faq.question: Can I unsend an email in Gmail?
faq.answer: Only for a short window. Undo Send can be set to 5, 10, 20 or 30 seconds. Once a message is delivered, Undo Send does not recall it. Google's page does not say what happens to delivered messages.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my Gmail messages?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text, points at things and guides you one click at a time. It does not click buttons for you. You read the draft and press send yourself.

faq.question: What does Lazur see on my screen?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Can I schedule an email in Gmail on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Scheduled send holds an email for a later time, and Gmail can hold up to 100 at once. Cancelling a scheduled email turns it into a draft. Google's steps describe the iPhone and iPad app, so use the browser guide linked in this page for Mac.
